name: Samuel Ellis
current_role: Early-stage software investor; partner at Scout Ventures (per 2022 interviews; current status not confirmed)
profile: Sam Ellis is a West Point graduate (operations research) and former Army intelligence officer at U.S. Cyber Command who co-founded Dutchie, the cannabis e-commerce/POS platform later valued at about $3.75B. He built Dutchie's first software version, then moved into venture investing as a partner at Scout Ventures, leading SaaS pre-seed and seed deals.
interesting_fact: He single-handedly wrote the first version of Dutchie's online cannabis marketplace software while coming out of a military cyber role, coding in his spare time.
deep_cut_fact: Before Dutchie he served as a software developer and intelligence leader at U.S. Cyber Command after studying operations research and applied statistics at West Point; he has said he spotted great engineers as people who 'love the game'.
notes: Low public profile; the less-visible co-founder next to Ross and Zach Lipson. Veteran-focused VC (Scout Ventures) is the natural route; current Scout role unverified on its team page. Podcasts: Travis Makes Money #717 (2022), Those Who Dare (May 2022).

name: Pedro Castillo
current_role: Founder of Onum, now Falcon Onum inside CrowdStrike (deal announced Aug 2025, reported ~$290M); co-founder of Devo
profile: Spanish engineer Pedro (del) Castillo co-founded Devo (originally Logtrust) in Madrid in 2011, a cloud-native security data analytics platform that became Spain's first cybersecurity unicorn; he served as CEO and then about 11 years as CTO. In 2022-23 he founded Onum, a real-time security data pipeline company, which CrowdStrike agreed to buy in 2025 to feed its Falcon Next-Gen SIEM.
interesting_fact: CrowdStrike's 2025 purchase of Onum (reported at $290M) gave Castillo a second security exit after Devo; he said pipelines should 'transform data into real-time intelligence', not just move it.
deep_cut_fact: Before Devo he was security tech director, then CTO and head of tech innovation at Bankinter, where back in 2001 his team built an on-prem system to collect all the data the bank generated, the seed of the Devo idea. Devo spent two years building product before launching and came within days of running out of cash.

public_contacts.value: https://www.crowdstrike.com (onum.com now redirects to CrowdStrike's Falcon Onum page)

notes: Also appears as Pedro del Castillo / Pedro Muros Castillo. Since the CrowdStrike deal, CrowdStrike press relations is likely the route; his post-acquisition title not verified. MWC Barcelona speaker. Do not confuse with Peru's former president Pedro Castillo.

name: Alexandre Yazdi
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Voodoo (Paris)
profile: Alexandre Yazdi, an engineering graduate (Polytech Nancy), co-founded Paris-based Voodoo with Laurent Ritter around 2012-13. Voodoo became one of the world's largest mobile game publishers through hyper-casual hits, backed by Goldman Sachs and Tencent at a ~$2B valuation, and has since expanded into consumer apps, including the social apps Wizz and BeReal.
interesting_fact: In June 2024 Voodoo bought French social app BeReal for a headline €500M, with Yazdi saying the aim was to refocus BeReal on growth and add advertising to move it toward profitability.
deep_cut_fact: Voodoo's very first app was a trivia game called 'Quiz Run', which passed 10 million downloads; by early 2016 the company had raised only about €1M in total.
notes: Keeps a fairly low personal media profile; company press office is the cleanest route. Some 2026 reports link him to buying a stake in DC Company (Konbini/Le Gorafi) but that is unverified here.

name: Matt Vincett
current_role: Longtime CEO of LifeMiles / Avianca Chief Loyalty Officer (2010 to at least late 2023); current role unverified after Avianca named new LifeMiles leadership in 2025
profile: Matt Vincett built LifeMiles, the Avianca-TACA frequent-flyer programme, as its CEO from 2010, launching it in March 2011 and leading its 2015 carve-out and partial sale to Advent International at a valuation of about $1B+. Avianca bought the whole business back in 2020. LifeMiles had more than 11 million members in 2023 and earns most of its money selling miles to banks and retailers.
interesting_fact: He describes LifeMiles as a business that sells miles to banks, partners and retailers more than an airline perk; by 2023 it had 11M+ members and co-branded cards in 10 countries.
deep_cut_fact: Before LifeMiles he was an airline man at TACA, serving as Commercial VP, VP of TACA's regional airlines and Director of Strategy & Business Development (per Avianca IR management bio).
notes: In Feb 2025 Avianca named Valeria Yglesias SVP Loyalty & managing director of LifeMiles, and later Jaime Manso to lead LifeMiles, so Vincett has probably moved on; his bio is gone from Avianca's current IR page (the TACA background came from an earlier version). Very low public profile; LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Jonathan Webb
current_role: Co-founder of Pharmapacks (later renamed Packable); co-founder and CEO of Packable per directory profiles; current activity unverified
profile: Jonathan Webb is one of five co-founders of Pharmapacks (2010, New York), which grew from a Bronx pharmacy operation into one of Amazon's largest US third-party sellers of health and beauty products and was valued at about $1B. It was renamed Packable, an e-commerce enablement company, and he is listed as its co-founder and CEO. His background is in spirits and luxury marketing and sales.
interesting_fact: Pharmapacks went from a Bronx retail pharmacy to one of the biggest sellers on Amazon in the US, built by a small group of friends.
deep_cut_fact: Before e-commerce, he co-founded LeSutra, a sparkling liqueur launched in 2012 with music producer Timbaland and Grey Goose co-founder Tom Bruno, with fellow future Pharmapacks co-founder Adam Berkowitz.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Packable (ex-Pharmapacks) went through Chapter 11 in 2022 after a planned SPAC deal fell through, so avoid framing outreach around the company's valuation. LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Mikki Nasch
current_role: Co-founder of Evidation Health (former SVP Commercial/business development); current role unverified
profile: Mikki Nasch is a serial tech executive who co-founded Evidation Health (2012) with Christine Lemke, Luca Foschini and Alessio Signorini. Evidation runs a consumer health app that lets millions of people share wearable and app data for research, and sells real-world evidence to pharma and payers; it was valued at about $1B. Earlier she held senior roles at Fair Isaac, BackWeb and Sense Networks.
interesting_fact: She argues 'between-care' data from wearables and apps should shape drug development from early trials through payer access, so the patient's voice reaches the people deciding reimbursement.
deep_cut_fact: Before Evidation she was EVP of business development at Sense Networks, a New York location-analytics startup co-founded with MIT's Alex 'Sandy' Pentland. Newsweek put it on its cover as 'The Next Google', and its Citysense app mapped nightlife hotspots from phone and taxi GPS data. Christine Lemke, her later Evidation co-founder, was its COO.
notes: Low public profile; Crunchbase lists her Evidation role in the past tense and her location as Canada. Christine Lemke (CEO) is Evidation's public face. LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Matthew Strongin
current_role: Co-founder, CFO and director of The Fynder Group (Nature's Fynd), Chicago
profile: Matthew Strongin is one of six founders of Nature's Fynd (The Fynder Group, formerly Sustainable Bioproducts, 2012) and its long-time CFO; he came from venture capital and banking. The Chicago company makes 'Fy' protein by fermenting a fungus from Yellowstone's hot springs and raised money from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, SoftBank, ADM and Danone at a valuation above $1B.
interesting_fact: The company's 'Fy' protein comes from a fungus (Fusarium strain flavolapis) found in Yellowstone's geothermal springs during a NASA-funded study of life in extreme environments; NASA later funded work on growing it for astronauts.
deep_cut_fact: Nature's Fynd started life in 2012 as Sustainable Bioproducts, trying to turn the Yellowstone microbe into biodiesel before pivoting to food, and it pays Yellowstone a share of profits for the right to harvest from the park.
notes: Behind-the-scenes finance co-founder; no interviews found. CEO Thomas Jonas is the public face. The deep-cut fact is about the company, not him personally. Also listed as founder of Lotic Labs (per aggregators, unverified).

name: Kit Dobyns
current_role: Co-founder of Cayaba Care (home-based maternity care, Philadelphia); co-founder of TrialSpark (now Formation Bio)
profile: Kit Dobyns, a Cornell graduate and Rhodes Scholar, co-founded TrialSpark in 2016 with Benjamine Liu and Linhao Zhang to make clinical trials faster and cheaper. The company, renamed Formation Bio in 2023, became an AI-driven drug developer valued at over $1B. He left in 2019 and co-founded Cayaba Care, which sends community care navigators to pregnant Medicaid patients at home.
interesting_fact: TrialSpark's origin is a dorm assignment: Liu and Dobyns were roommates at the Rhodes Scholar pre-orientation programme at Oxford.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving TrialSpark he moved from drug trials to maternal health, co-founding Cayaba Care with ER physician Olan Soremekun. It launched in Aug 2021 with $3.2M led by Flare Capital to cut maternal morbidity for underserved women through home visits between OB appointments.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. His current title at Cayaba is not confirmed. Best route is probably LinkedIn or via Cayaba Care.

name: Bryan Pelz
current_role: Founder & CEO, Bootloader Studio (spatial computing/Vision Pro apps, team mostly in Vietnam); co-founder and former CEO of VNG
profile: Bryan Pelz is an American entrepreneur who co-founded VinaGame (now VNG) in Vietnam around 2004-05 with Le Hong Minh and was CEO in its early years, backed by IDG Ventures. VNG became Vietnam's first tech unicorn (games, Zalo messenger, ZaloPay), valued at about $2B. He stayed on VNG's board for years and since 2022 has run Bootloader Studio, which builds apps for Apple Vision Pro.
interesting_fact: Bootloader's Vision Pro virtual-pet meditation game Pawz was an Apple Design Award 2025 finalist in the Innovation category.
deep_cut_fact: Korean coverage of VNG's origins casts the founding as a duo: Le Hong Minh, a gamer educated in Australia, and Pelz, an American who had already taken a startup through an IPO in France. They spotted online games as Vietnam got broadband, and 'Vina' in VinaGame refers to Vietnam.
notes: Based in Vietnam and active on LinkedIn, where he posts about Bootloader and Vision Pro events in Ho Chi Minh City; that is the best route. Le Hong Minh is VNG's better-known founder and CEO. Bootloader's official web domain is unconfirmed (bootloader.studio is not theirs).

name: Cao Jiang
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Sensors Data (神策数据), Beijing
profile: Cao Jiang (曹犟) is co-founder and CTO of Sensors Data, a Beijing analytics company founded in May 2015 by former Baidu big-data engineers led by CEO Sang Wenfeng. It sells user-behaviour analytics and marketing-automation software that can be deployed on a customer's own servers. Before Sensors he worked in Baidu's big-data department; the company reached a valuation of about $1B.
interesting_fact: Sensors Data was built on the founders' Baidu experience: the pitch was a 'big data platform plus Baidu Analytics' hybrid that customers could install privately, and it opened with a 6M yuan angel round in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: The team's first startup idea wasn't analytics: Sang Wenfeng proposed a matchmaking-event website using big data to match couples. He sent the plan to Cao Jiang and others, and each agreed to put in 5,000 yuan, before a Tsinghua alumni startup contest steered them elsewhere.
notes: Chinese-language profile; speaks at Sensors' annual data-driven conference. CEO Sang Wenfeng is the company's public face. Reports say Cao was in Baidu's big-data department 2008-2014 (single source).

name: Cody Friesen
current_role: Founder & CEO, SOURCE Global PBC (formerly Zero Mass Water), Scottsdale AZ; associate professor of materials science, Arizona State University (as of 2022)
profile: Cody Friesen is a materials scientist (ASU BS, MIT PhD) who founded Zero Mass Water, now SOURCE Global. Its solar 'hydropanels' pull drinking water out of the air and are deployed in about 45 countries; the company was valued around $1B. He previously co-founded Fluidic Energy (now NantEnergy), which built rechargeable zinc-air batteries for off-grid power and raised over $150M.
interesting_fact: He won the 2019 $500,000 Lemelson-MIT Prize, the largest US cash prize for invention, for work on both fresh water (hydropanels) and reliable energy (metal-air batteries) for the developing world; he also won ASU's McNulty Prize in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Arizona, and the Lemelson-MIT profile credits the state's farmland and desert, including irrigation canals built by Native Americans, with sparking his early interest in science and environmental technology.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/water-tech podcast: deep background in batteries and off-grid power. Henry Crown Fellow (Aspen Institute). ASU faculty channels and SOURCE's website are the routes; no published press email found. 2025-26 status not checked because the search budget ran out.

name: Doron Somech
current_role: Co-founder of Unit (embedded-banking infrastructure, NYC/Tel Aviv); apparently now building Submilli, a secure runtime for AI code agents
profile: Doron Somech is a Tel Aviv software engineer listed as a co-founder of Unit, the banking-as-a-service platform (founded 2019 with CEO Itai Damti) that lets software companies embed accounts, cards and payments; it was valued at about $1B. He no longer appears on Unit's leadership page, and his GitHub now points to Submilli, an open-source WebAssembly sandbox runtime for 'code-mode' AI agents.
interesting_fact: His newest project, Submilli, runs code written by AI agents in isolated WebAssembly sandboxes with no network or file access by default, enforcing permissions on each call with an audit trail.
notes: The GitHub user somdoron (Doron Somech, Tel Aviv, member of the ZeroMQ org, site submilli.ai) is very likely the same person; he is widely known in open source as a ZeroMQ/NetMQ maintainer, but I could not source-confirm the NetMQ link or tie Unit to him from a primary page (search budget exhausted), so that is left out of the facts. Unit's current about page lists Itai Damti as its only founder.

name: Sumeet Kapahi
current_role: Co-founder, Lenskart (Indian omnichannel eyewear company); current executive title not confirmed
profile: Sumeet Kapahi joined Peyush Bansal and Amit Chaudhary as Lenskart's third co-founder in September 2011, coming from another eyewear brand. Lenskart grew from a Delhi online eyewear store into India's largest eyewear retailer, with its own manufacturing and thousands of stores. It launched an IPO in October 2025 at a reported valuation of up to about $8B.
interesting_fact: Lenskart launched its Indian IPO in October 2025 to raise up to about $828M, at a valuation Reuters put at up to $8B; it started as an online store run by Valyoo Technologies, a company Bansal registered at his parents' home in Delhi.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike his co-founders, Kapahi was an eyewear-industry insider: he was working for another eyewear brand when he joined the young venture in 2011.
notes: Low-profile operator; Peyush Bansal (Shark Tank India judge) is the public face. As a listed company Lenskart publishes an investor/company-secretary contact in its exchange filings (not retrieved here). Search budget ran out, so his current title wasn't verified.

name: Roy Chung
current_role: Listed as a founder of Apollo.io (sales intelligence and engagement platform); current role unknown
profile: Roy Chung is listed as a founder of Apollo.io, the San Francisco sales-intelligence and outreach platform founded in 2015 (growing out of the earlier startup Braingenie) and valued at about $1.6B in 2023. Apollo's own site now names only Tim Zheng (CEO) and Ray Li (CTO) as founders, and I could not find a primary source on Chung's role or current activity.
interesting_fact: Apollo says it has 5M+ users, 100K+ paying customers and a database of 240M+ contacts across 30M+ companies.
notes: Identity not confirmed: Apollo's about page lists only Tim Zheng and Ray Li as founders, so Chung was probably an early co-founder who left. Kept minimal (search budget exhausted). Use Apollo's press contact only if he is still connected to the company.

name: Chris Simair
current_role: Co-founder, President & Head of Operations, Neo Financial (Calgary)
profile: Chris Simair co-founded SkipTheDishes with his brother Josh in Saskatoon in 2012. The food-delivery app grew into a top Canadian brand and was sold to Just Eat in 2016 for about $200M. He and fellow Skip co-founders Andrew Chau, Jeff Adamson and Kris Read then started Neo Financial, a Calgary fintech offering credit cards, savings and rewards, valued at about C$2B+ (~US$2B).
interesting_fact: Neo Financial ranked No. 1 on The Globe and Mail's 2024 list of Canada's Top Growing Companies.
deep_cut_fact: SkipTheDishes began in Saskatoon before moving its head office to Winnipeg. The founding team was largely family and friends: brothers Chris, Josh and Dan Simair plus university friends, and Chris and Andrew Chau left after the Just Eat sale to go on to build Neo.
notes: Operations-focused co-founder; CEO Andrew Chau is Neo's usual spokesperson. Neo's media inbox is the cleanest route. Valuation figures not re-verified (search budget exhausted).

name: Andrew Scharenberg
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Umoja Biopharma (Seattle)
profile: Andrew Scharenberg, MD, is co-founder and CEO of Umoja Biopharma, a Seattle clinical-stage biotech he started with Ryan Crisman and scientific co-founder Philip Low (Purdue). Umoja is developing 'in vivo' CAR-T therapies, in which its VivoVec lentiviral delivery platform engineers a patient's T cells inside the body instead of in a lab; it was valued at about $1B.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Umoja got FDA clearance for UB-VV400, which it calls the industry's first known CD22-directed in vivo CAR-T, and its first clinical data were chosen for an oral presentation at ASH 2026 (Dec).
notes: Timely hook: first in vivo CAR-T clinical data at ASH in December 2026. Earlier academic and gene-editing career (Seattle Children's/UW) not verified here because the search budget ran out. Scientific co-founder Philip Low died in early 2026, so avoid that in outreach.

name: Arik Faingold
current_role: Listed as a founder of Pentera (formerly Pcysys), Israeli automated security-validation company; current role unknown
profile: Arik Faingold is listed as a founder of Pentera, the Tel Aviv/Boston company founded in 2015 (as Pcysys) that sells an autonomous penetration-testing / exposure-validation platform and was valued at about $1B in its 2022 round. Pentera's current site names only Dr. Arik Liberzon as founder and Amitai Ratzon as CEO, and does not mention Faingold.
interesting_fact: Pentera now sells AI agents that run attack simulations against live production web apps within customer-set guardrails; this is the 'automated pentesting' category it helped create in 2015.

public_contacts.value: https://pentera.io/newsroom/ (press contact obfuscated; company Contact Us page)

notes: Identity not confirmed from a primary source: Pentera's about page credits only Arik Liberzon as founder. Faingold was probably an early co-founder or executive at Pcysys who has since left. Kept minimal (search budget exhausted).

name: Gabriel Otte
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Freenome (South San Francisco, AI blood-based cancer detection); current role not verified
profile: Gabriel Otte co-founded Freenome in 2014 with Riley Ennis and led it as CEO through its early venture rounds (a16z, Google Ventures, Roche), building an AI/multi-omics blood test for early cancer detection; it was valued at over $1B. Freenome later licensed its colorectal cancer blood test to Exact Sciences and listed on Nasdaq (FRNM) in July 2026 via a SPAC merger. Otte no longer appears in the company's leadership or press materials.
interesting_fact: Freenome, the company he co-founded, began trading on Nasdaq as FRNM on July 21, 2026, through a business combination with Perceptive Capital Solutions Corp.
notes: Freenome's current materials name only Riley Ennis as co-founder; Otte's departure and current activity could not be checked (search budget exhausted). Freenome's media (ryan@gracegroup.us) and IR (freenome@gilmartinir.com) contacts are company channels, not his, so they are not listed as his contacts.

name: Li Jingpeng
current_role: Listed as founder of Desano (Shanghai Desano Pharmaceuticals / 上海迪赛诺医药集团); current title not verified
profile: Li Jingpeng is listed as founder of Desano, a Shanghai Zhangjiang pharmaceutical group founded in 1996. Desano makes antiretroviral (HIV) and antimalarial APIs and finished drugs plus CDMO services, holds WHO/FDA/EMA approvals, and is one of the world's major suppliers of HIV drug ingredients; it was valued at about $1B. Desano's own website does not name its founder, so his role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Since 2003 Desano has supplied drugs to China's national HIV/AIDS treatment programme every year (23 consecutive years), and several of its anti-HIV APIs carry WHO, FDA and EMA approvals for global public-health supply.
notes: Identity unconfirmed: Desano's Chinese name is 迪赛诺 and the founder's Chinese name was not verified (search budget exhausted). Private and Chinese-language; the company inbox is the only published route.

name: Michael Broukhim
current_role: Co-founder of FabFitFun (Los Angeles lifestyle subscription-box company); current title not verified
profile: Michael Broukhim co-founded FabFitFun, the Los Angeles company behind the seasonal beauty, wellness and lifestyle subscription box plus member e-commerce shop, with his brother Daniel Broukhim and editor Katie Rosen Kitchens; the business was valued at about $1B. Details of his current role and background could not be verified in this pass.
